```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, comment = "")
```

This notebook downloads the SEAMAP plankton archive and builds the three tables used in the
analysis, which are sampling effort, cobia catch records, and individual larval lengths.

```{r packages}
library(tidyverse); library(suncalc)

dir_raw     <- "data/raw"
dir_seamap  <- file.path(dir_raw, "seamap")
dir_derived <- "data/derived"
for (p in c(dir_seamap, dir_derived)) dir.create(p, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

BOX    <- list(lon = c(-98, -80), lat = c(18, 31))   # study area
FATHOM <- 1.8288                                     # DEPTH_SSTA is recorded in fathoms
```

# Download

The Gulf States Marine Fisheries Commission distributes the whole plankton archive as one zip file
and updates it periodically. This chunk runs only if the tables are missing. The first download is
a few hundred MB.

```{r download, eval = !all(file.exists(file.path("data/raw/seamap", c("STAREC.csv", "ISTRWK.csv", "ISARWK.csv", "ILFRWK.csv"))))}
URL  <- "https://seamapdata.gsmfc.org/files/SEAMAPPlanktonCSV.zip"
zipf <- file.path(dir_raw, "SEAMAPPlanktonCSV.zip")
want <- c("STAREC.csv", "ISTRWK.csv", "ISARWK.csv", "ILFRWK.csv")

if (!file.exists(zipf)) { options(timeout = 3600); download.file(URL, zipf, mode = "wb") }
inside <- unzip(zipf, list = TRUE)$Name
for (f in want[!file.exists(file.path(dir_seamap, want))]) {
  unzip(zipf, files = inside[basename(inside) == f][1], exdir = dir_seamap, junkpaths = TRUE)
}
writeLines(c(paste("source:", URL), paste("downloaded:", format(Sys.time()))),
           file.path(dir_seamap, "SOURCE.txt"))
```

Four tables are used. They are linked by `V_C_P` (vessel, cruise, station), `V_C_P_S` (adds the
sample), and `V_C_P_S_CAT` (adds the catalog number), which links a length to a catch record.

| table | one row per | fields used |
|---|---|---|
| `STAREC` | station | date, time, position, depth, gears deployed |
| `ISTRWK` | plankton sample | gear code, mesh, volume filtered, sorted flag |
| `ISARWK` | taxon within a sample | counts, aliquot |
| `ILFRWK` | measured larva | length |

Every column is read as text, and the byte order mark at the start of the first header is removed.

```{r reader}
read_seamap <- function(f) {
  read_csv(file.path(dir_seamap, f), col_types = cols(.default = col_character()),
           show_col_types = FALSE, name_repair = "minimal") %>%
    rename_with(~ str_remove(.x, "^﻿"))
}
```

# Stations

Positions are stored as degrees and minutes in separate columns. `DEPTH_SSTA` is in fathoms, not
meters. `TEMP_SSURF` is surface temperature in degrees Celsius and is entered as zero when no reading
was taken, so values outside 5 to 36 degrees are set to missing. The station table has no salinity
field.

`TIME_MIL` is clock time in the time zone given by `TIME_ZN`. Early cruises mostly recorded local
Central or Eastern time, and from about 2000 nearly every station was recorded in GMT. A tow at 3 pm
local time is recorded as 2000 GMT, so reading it as local time would place it at 8 pm. Each time is
therefore converted to GMT, and a station is classed as night when the sun was below the horizon at
that time and position, using the `suncalc` package. Zone 9 ("other") and impossible times are set
to missing.

```{r stations}
TEMP_OK <- c(5, 36)                                  # outside this range TEMP_SSURF is a sentinel
TZ_OFFSET <- c("1" = -5, "2" = -4, "3" = -6, "4" = -5, "5" = -4, "6" = -3, "8" = 0)  # hours from GMT

starec <- read_seamap("STAREC.csv") %>%
  transmute(v_c_p    = V_C_P,
            date     = as.Date(substr(MO_DAY_YR, 1, 10)),
            time_mil = TIME_MIL,
            time_zn  = TIME_ZN,
            gears    = GEARS,
            lat = as.numeric(S_LATD) + as.numeric(S_LATM) / 60,
            lon = (as.numeric(S_LOND) + as.numeric(S_LONM) / 60) * if_else(S_LONH == "W", -1, 1),
            sta_depth_m = as.numeric(DEPTH_SSTA) * FATHOM,
            temp_surf = as.numeric(TEMP_SSURF)) %>%
  mutate(temp_surf = if_else(temp_surf >= TEMP_OK[1] & temp_surf <= TEMP_OK[2], temp_surf, NA_real_)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(date), !is.na(lat), !is.na(lon)) %>%
  arrange(v_c_p, date) %>%
  distinct(v_c_p, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%    # V_C_P should be unique; keep the first if not
  mutate(hh = suppressWarnings(as.integer(substr(str_pad(time_mil, 4, "left", "0"), 1, 2))),
         mm = suppressWarnings(as.integer(substr(str_pad(time_mil, 4, "left", "0"), 3, 4))),
         time_utc = if_else(hh <= 23 & mm <= 59,
                            as.POSIXct(date, tz = "UTC") + (hh + mm / 60 - TZ_OFFSET[time_zn]) * 3600,
                            as.POSIXct(NA, tz = "UTC")),
         night = getSunlightPosition(data = data.frame(date = time_utc, lat = lat, lon = lon))$altitude < 0) %>%
  select(-hh, -mm)

sprintf("%d stations; surface temperature on %d (%.1f%%)",
        nrow(starec), sum(!is.na(starec$temp_surf)),
        100 * mean(!is.na(starec$temp_surf)))
count(starec, time_zn, night)
```

# Effort

Gear codes follow Section II of the survey documentation. `SORT_IST` records whether a sample was
sorted. Only sorted samples could produce an identified larva, so only sorted samples count as
effort in the catch rates.

Only the standard SEAMAP gears count as effort, as defined in the survey documentation. These are
the 61- or 60-cm bongo with 0.333-mm mesh (gear 01 or 17, mesh 03) and the single or double neuston
net with 0.947-mm mesh (gear 03 or 08, mesh 09). Bongo and neuston nets with other meshes are
labeled non-standard. Their larvae stay on the distribution map but are left out of every catch
rate. This removes 36 cobia larvae, 19 from bongo nets and 17 from neuston nets with mesh 05.

```{r effort}
GEAR <- c("01" = "Bongo", "17" = "Bongo", "11" = "Bongo", "14" = "Bongo", "05" = "Bongo",
          "12" = "Bongo", "13" = "Bongo", "15" = "Bongo",
          "03" = "Neuston", "08" = "Neuston",
          "07" = "Tucker trawl", "09" = "MOCNESS", "02" = "Ring", "04" = "Ring",
          "16" = "Methot", "06" = "Other")
SORTED <- c("1", "2", "4", "D")

istrwk <- read_seamap("ISTRWK.csv") %>%
  transmute(v_c_p = V_C_P, v_c_p_s = V_C_P_S,   # V_C_P is 9 characters on a few stations
            gear = GEAR[GEAR_ICD], sort_ist = SORT_IST, vol_filt_m3 = as.numeric(VOL_FILT),
            standard = (GEAR_ICD %in% c("01", "17") & MESH_ICD == "03") |
                       (GEAR_ICD %in% c("03", "08") & MESH_ICD == "09")) %>%
  mutate(gear = if_else(gear %in% c("Bongo", "Neuston") & !standard,
                        paste(gear, "(non-standard)"), gear)) %>%
  select(-standard)
count(istrwk, gear, name = "samples")

# One deployment per station per gear class: a bongo pair and a double neuston frame each count once.
effort <- istrwk %>%
  filter(gear %in% c("Bongo", "Neuston"), sort_ist %in% SORTED) %>%
  distinct(v_c_p, gear) %>%
  inner_join(starec, by = "v_c_p") %>%
  filter(lon >= BOX$lon[1], lon <= BOX$lon[2], lat >= BOX$lat[1], lat <= BOX$lat[2]) %>%
  mutate(year  = year(date),
         month = month(date),
         region = case_when(
           sta_depth_m <= 0 | sta_depth_m > 200                    ~ NA_character_,
           lat >= 26 & lat <= 30.5 & lon >= -98 & lon < -88        ~ "Texas-Louisiana shelf",
           lat >= 25 & lat <= 30.5 & lon >= -88 & lon <  -82       ~ "West Florida shelf"))
write_csv(effort, file.path(dir_derived, "effort.csv"), na = "")
count(effort, gear, name = "deployments")
```

Sampling differs through the year. The spring survey samples the open Gulf and the fall survey
samples the shelf. June and July plankton samples come from the summer shrimp trawl survey, which
works west of 88 W and stopped collecting plankton after 2016.

```{r effort-by-month}
effort %>% filter(sta_depth_m > 0, sta_depth_m <= 200) %>%
  mutate(era = if_else(year <= 2016, "1982-2016", "2017-2024")) %>%
  count(era, month) %>% pivot_wider(names_from = era, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)
```

# Cobia catch

The taxon match is anchored to the start of the name so that *Poromitra megalops*, a melamphaid
with the same species name, is not included. Counts refer to the sorted part of each sample, so
each count is multiplied by the inverse of its aliquot.

```{r catch}
ALIQ_MULT <- c("1/1" = 1, "1/2" = 2, "1/4" = 4, "1/8" = 8)

catch <- read_seamap("ISARWK.csv") %>%
  filter(str_detect(toupper(TAXON), "^RACHYCENTR")) %>%
  transmute(v_c_p = substr(V_C_P_S, 1, 10), v_c_p_s = V_C_P_S, v_c_p_s_cat = V_C_P_S_CAT,
            taxon = TAXON, aliquot = ALIQUOT, sort_isa = SORT_ISA,
            n_sorted = coalesce(as.numeric(MEAS), 0) + coalesce(as.numeric(NOT_MEAS), 0),
            n_total  = n_sorted * coalesce(ALIQ_MULT[ALIQUOT], 1))
count(catch, taxon, wt = n_total, name = "larvae")
sprintf("%.0f larvae sorted, %.0f after the aliquot correction, %d records sub-sampled",
        sum(catch$n_sorted), sum(catch$n_total), sum(catch$aliquot != "1/1"))
```

# Lengths

Size classes use round numbers close to the tertiles of measured length. They describe size only and
are not developmental stages, because the specimens were not re-examined and no age-length
relationship has been published for wild cobia larvae.

```{r lengths}
SIZE_LEVELS <- c("Small (<5 mm)", "Medium (5-15 mm)", "Large (>15 mm)")

lengths <- read_seamap("ILFRWK.csv") %>%
  filter(V_C_P_S_CAT %in% catch$v_c_p_s_cat) %>%
  transmute(v_c_p_s_cat = V_C_P_S_CAT, length_mm = as.numeric(LENGTH)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(length_mm)) %>%
  mutate(size = factor(case_when(length_mm <  5  ~ SIZE_LEVELS[1],
                                 length_mm <= 15 ~ SIZE_LEVELS[2],
                                 TRUE            ~ SIZE_LEVELS[3]), levels = SIZE_LEVELS))
write_csv(lengths, file.path(dir_derived, "lengths.csv"))

round(quantile(lengths$length_mm, c(0, 1/3, 0.5, 2/3, 1)), 1)
count(lengths, size)
```

Each larva is classed by its own length rather than by the tow median. A median hides mixed catches,
because a tow with larvae of 2.4 and 6.0 mm has a median of 4.2 mm and no longer shows the 2.4 mm
larva.

```{r records}
by_rec <- lengths %>%
  group_by(v_c_p_s_cat) %>%
  summarise(n_meas = n(), len_med = median(length_mm), len_min = min(length_mm),
            n_small = sum(size == SIZE_LEVELS[1]),
            n_mid   = sum(size == SIZE_LEVELS[2]),
            n_big   = sum(size == SIZE_LEVELS[3]), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(has_small = n_small > 0,
         # the class holding most of the tow, for one colour per symbol on a map
         size_class = factor(SIZE_LEVELS[max.col(cbind(n_small, n_mid, n_big),
                                                 ties.method = "first")], levels = SIZE_LEVELS))

records <- catch %>%
  left_join(by_rec, by = "v_c_p_s_cat") %>%
  left_join(istrwk %>% select(v_c_p_s, gear, sort_ist, vol_filt_m3), by = "v_c_p_s") %>%
  inner_join(starec, by = "v_c_p") %>%
  mutate(year  = year(date),
         month = month(date),
         has_small = coalesce(has_small, FALSE),
         region = case_when(
           sta_depth_m <= 0 | sta_depth_m > 200              ~ NA_character_,
           lat >= 26 & lat <= 30.5 & lon >= -98 & lon < -88  ~ "Texas-Louisiana shelf",
           lat >= 25 & lat <= 30.5 & lon >= -88 & lon <  -82 ~ "West Florida shelf"))
write_csv(records, file.path(dir_derived, "cobia_records.csv"), na = "")

gulf <- records %>%
  filter(lon >= BOX$lon[1], lon <= BOX$lon[2], lat >= BOX$lat[1], lat <= BOX$lat[2])
sprintf("%d records, %.0f larvae; %d records and %.0f larvae in the study box; %d measured",
        nrow(records), sum(records$n_total), nrow(gulf), sum(gulf$n_total),
        sum(gulf$n_meas, na.rm = TRUE))
```
